questions: Should the function raise an exception if the file exists but is not a valid DLL (e.g., a text file with .dll extension), or should it still return metadata from the file system?
If the DLL's internal version information is available (e.g., via ctypes.WinDLL or pefile), should it be used to override or supplement the file system metadata?
Should the returned DLL name be the full filepath, the basename, or the internal name from the DLL object (lib._name)?
If the file system metadata (e.g., st_ctime) is not available on the current OS, should the function fallback, raise an error, or use a default?
Should the function close the loaded DLL (e.g., via ctypes.windll.kernel32.FreeLibrary) after retrieving metadata to avoid resource leaks?
Is the file size expected in bytes, or should it be formatted (e.g., KB, MB)?
Should the function handle symbolic links to DLL files by returning metadata of the link or the target?
If the DLL loading fails due to missing dependencies, should the function still return file metadata before raising an error?
